Ideas (not decided; newest first): - **Our own Lagos motion from video, and AI video** (owner, 23 Oct). Motion2MixamoRig (github.com/MaxLiu22/Motion2MixamoRig, code Apache-2.0, experimental): a video of one person, whole body in frame, becomes motion on a Mixamo character (.glb for Blender/Unreal); Blender add-on tested on Apple Silicon, slow but fine on CPU (3-15 min per 30 s clip). Fills the gap Mixamo's library leaves: Lagos-only moves (basin on the head, conductor hanging off the door, frying akara, bargaining, climbing on an okada), filmed by the owner or friends who agree, never strangers' clips. **Catch:** it needs SMPL-X, non-commercial by default (a commercial licence is a separate deal), and the GVHMR weights have their own licence: use it for study and prototypes (person spots), then licence it or redo final animations with a sale-cleared tool before shipping. To set up (needs the owner's OK): repo + Python packages; about 5 GB of weights on first run; the SMPL-X file (owner signs up on the SMPL-X site); a Mixamo FBX from the owner's Adobe account. Mixamo itself: free library, retarget onto City Sample/MetaHuman in Unreal; usable in a shipped game, raw files not shared.

Lagos light: why the city looks different: The owner's observation: photos taken in Nigeria look different from photos taken abroad. The vibrancy and the feel of the light aren't the same.
